quote: The claimant must have an accurate model of the situation somewhere in their mind, because they can anticipate, in advance, exactly which experimental results they’ll need to excuse.
content: The claimant offers excuses after hearing proposed tests but before seeing their results; that is still anticipation in advance of the outcome. An on-demand rationalization must select which possible result to neutralize, so it does not eliminate every form of outcome expectation. Nevertheless, 'must have an accurate model' overstates what the story identifies: predicting an evidential threat does not prove a stable, consciously accessible hidden conviction that no dragon exists.

quote: Some philosophers have been much confused by such scenarios
content: A prior articulation supports the distinction's substance even when it defeats a claim to originality, and the essay already credits Dennett rather than claiming discovery from nothing. Fable's cited 2008 and 2014 works cannot establish that their formulations preceded this 2007 essay; its 1997 example can. The vague swipe at philosophers deserves criticism, but the existence of better-developed versions is not a refutation of the distinction being taught.

quote: not unless they are unusually capable of acknowledging their own lack of virtue
content: Wanting stronger faith or admitting partial doubt is not identical to admitting complete absence of belief while maintaining only the belief that one ought to believe. That distinction weakens Fable's attempt to treat all openly cultivated faith as a counterexample. Still, the essay supplies no evidence for the exceptional-virtue qualifier, which should be dropped rather than used to reclassify every contrary case.

quote: you may remember a time period when you first began to doubt Santa Claus’s existence, but you still believed that you were supposed to believe in Santa Claus, so you tried to deny the doubts
content: The sentence says that depending on childhood one may remember this experience, not that the modal child undergoes it. Predominantly neutral or positive reactions after discovery do not rule out earlier efforts to suppress doubt, either. Fable has not supplied the prevalence measure required to turn its description of the modal child's behavior into a refutation of this conditional invitation.

quote: the dragon-claimant anticipates as if there is no dragon in their garage, and makes excuses as if they believed in the belief
content: Commonness does not establish epistemic success. A person can hold both natural and supernatural explanations without contradiction if they make compatible claims, but switching between incompatible expectations does not become accurate because many people do it. The essay's evaluative question is whether avowals and anticipations remain answerable to evidence, not whether the configuration is statistically unusual.
